Draw the state of a lattice

Source: R/spatial-plot.R
abm_plot_lattice.Rd

A frame of a lattice model is a filter on the result tibble plus geom_raster(aes(.x, .y, fill = ...)), and every spatial model's figure starts the same way: pick the tick, keep the cells, fix the aspect ratio, drop the axes a grid of cells does not need. abm_plot_lattice() is that start. It returns an ordinary ggplot, so scales, labels, titles and facets are added to it as usual.

Usage

abm_plot_lattice(
  result,
  fill = NULL,
  tick = NULL,
  agents = FALSE,
  colour = NULL,
  shape = NULL,
  size = 1.2,
  colours = NULL
)

Arguments

result

An abm_run() result, or any data frame carrying .x and .y (for example several final frames bound together with a column saying which run each came from, to facet on).

fill

What colours a cell: a column or an expression over the cell's columns, as in ggplot2::aes(). Leave it out to draw the cells in a single neutral grey, for example under points. A cell whose value is NA (an empty cell) is drawn in the scale's na.value; give the scale na.translate = FALSE to leave it blank instead, which emits no warning.

tick

Which tick(s) to draw. The last recorded tick by default; several ticks are drawn as one facet each.

agents

Whether to draw the mobile agents over the cells.

colour

What colours a mobile agent: a column or an expression over the agent's columns. .group by default. A discrete value gets one colour per level; a numeric one gets a gradient.

shape

What shapes a mobile agent: a column or an expression over the agent's columns, or NULL for a filled circle.

size

The point size of a mobile agent, in ggplot2's units.

colours

The agents' colours: for a discrete colour, a vector of colours named by level (an unnamed one is taken in level order); for a numeric colour, the two ends of the gradient. NULL picks Okabe-Ito colours, or a light-to-dark blue gradient.

Value

A ggplot object. Needs the ggplot2 package.

Details

The wired group's rows are the cells; a row with a .cell is an agent standing on one. With agents = TRUE those are drawn over the cells as points, coloured by .group unless colour says otherwise, in the Okabe-Ito palette (colour-blind safe) unless colours says otherwise. The point layer comes with its colour scale, so to change the agents' colours pass colours rather than adding a second scale_colour_*(), which would replace it with a message.

Several ticks are drawn as one facet each, in a single row when there are six or fewer: a strip showing how the world evolved.

See also

abm_view_lattice() for the same frames as an interactive playback; abm_network() for the lattice itself; abm_move() for the agents standing on it.

Examples

life <- abm_setup(agents = abm_grid(dims = c(30, 30), alive = ~runif(n) < 0.3))
go <- abm_go(abm_neighbours(k ~ sum(alive)),
             abm_rules(alive ~ k == 3 | (alive & k == 2)))
r <- abm_run(life, go, ticks = 20, seed = 1, record = 10)
abm_plot_lattice(r, fill = alive, tick = c(0, 10, 20))
